finding_async_feature_is_INERT.severity: documentation defect, not a build defect
finding_async_feature_is_INERT.evidence: grep -rn 'feature = "async"' over crates/slate-kv-hal/src/ and crates/slate-kv-core/src/ returns ZERO hits. Only `feature = "embedded-storage-async"` gates anything in the HAL (the storage_async module at hal:63).
finding_async_feature_is_INERT.probe: A separate crate depending on both slate-kv-hal and slate-kv-core with default-features = false (async OFF in both) compiles a function generic over AsyncFlash, one over AsyncMonotonicCounter, a BlockingFlash construction, and task::yield_now(). Exit 0. So AsyncFlash/AsyncMonotonicCounter/BlockingFlash/BlockingCounter/YieldNow/block_on are UNCONDITIONALLY compiled regardless of the `async` feature.
finding_async_feature_is_INERT.consequence: Doc 018 §3 states the traits are 'gated behind feature = "async", default OFF' and §8 repeats it. That is not what the code does: the async HAL surface is always on. The bare-metal build pays for it unconditionally. The paper must not claim the async surface is opt-in.

finding_blocking_feature_DOES_gate.evidence: The same probe crate, extended to call Slate::commit() with slate-kv-core default-features = false, fails to compile: `error[E0599]: no method named commit found for mutable reference &mut Slate<..>` (rc=101). Adding --features slate-kv-core/blocking makes it compile (rc=0).

finding_embassy_demo_does_not_use_embass.severity: This invalidates doc 018 §9 step 11 and acceptance criterion 'Measured ESP32 max task jitter under seal+GC load reduced by >=8x versus blocking'. The instrument for that measurement does not exist.
evidence: targets/esp32/src/bin/embassy_demo.rs:4-5 — `use embassy_executor::Spawner;` and `use embassy_time::{Duration, Instant, Timer};` are COMMENTED OUT.
lines 32-66 — heartbeat_task() and jitter_logger_task(), the two #[embassy_executor::task] functions, are inside a /* ... */ block comment.
line 69 — entry point is `#[esp_hal::main] fn main() -> !`, a plain synchronous main, NOT #[embassy_executor::main].
lines 78-83 — in-source comments: 'we leave this as a template', 'In a real Embassy setup, we would start an executor here', spawner.spawn(..) calls commented out.
line 92-93 — flash and counter are wrapped in BlockingFlash / BlockingCounter, exactly as kv_demo does.
lines 107, 239, 253, 256, 259 — every engine call goes through slate_kv_core::task::block_on(..). No executor ever polls a Slate future.
line 30 — MAX_JITTER_US is #[allow(dead_code)]: the jitter metric the doc calls 'the headline claim of the feature' is never written.
finding_embassy_demo_does_not_use_embass.conclusion: embassy_demo is kv_demo's write loop driven by block_on, with the Embassy parts commented out. It exercises the async core through the blocking bridge, which is genuinely useful as a compile+run smoke test of the async engine on the real target, but it demonstrates neither concurrency nor DMA offload. The banner it prints, 'embassy_demo started (concurrency, not DMA offload)', overstates what the binary does.
finding_embassy_demo_does_not_use_embass.link_level_confirmation: llvm-nm on targets/esp32/target/riscv32imc-unknown-none-elf/release/embassy_demo: ZERO symbols from embassy_executor or embassy_time are linked in. Every 'embassy' substring in the symbol table is the crate-name suffix '12embassy_demo' in a Rust v0 mangled name belonging to slate_kv_core/slate_kv_hal generics. So the Embassy dependency declared in targets/esp32/Cargo.toml (embassy-executor 0.10.0, embassy-time 0.5.1) is compiled but entirely dead-stripped: the firmware contains no executor. Confirmed at link level, not just source level.
finding_embassy_demo_does_not_use_embass.async_core_IS_linked: Both binaries do link the async engine: llvm-nm shows monomorphised block_on / commit_async / index_update_offset_async / gc::reindex_update_offset over BlockingFlash<EspFlash>, BlockingCounter<EspCounter>, CryptoSealer. The async state machines are real generated code on the RISC-V target, driven by block_on. That part of doc 018 holds on hardware-targeted code.

derived.interpretation: embassy_demo's .text is 9368 B SMALLER than kv_demo's. kv_demo carries a UART command interpreter and a self-check harness that embassy_demo does not; embassy_demo's loop is a bare write/seal/compact cycle. Because BOTH binaries use the blocking facade over the same async core, this number does NOT measure the flash cost of async. The paper CANNOT state an async-vs-blocking firmware size delta from these two binaries. Measuring that would require a genuinely async build of the same application logic, which does not exist in the tree.
derived.ram_note: The ~78 KB of .data+.bss is dominated by the statically-allocated engine buffers each binary declares identically (HOT_BUF 4096 + COLD_BUF 4096 + INDEX_SLOTS 2048*4 u32 = 32768 + CKPT_BUF 35000 = 75960 B, verified at kv_demo.rs:21-24 and embassy_demo.rs:25-28), not by async. The 60 B .data difference between them is not attributable to async. .stack (~238 KB) is a linker-reserved region, not an allocation.
